options.text: The government wanted people to follow the policy of' Be Indian; Buy Indian'
Because foreign goods were costly and meant loss of precious foreign exchange
Government policy was directed towards protection of domestic industries from foreign competition
Government wanted to preserve Indian culture and to avoid influence of foreign culture

questions.explanation: As per ICAI Study Material (Paper 4: Business Economics, Chapter 10: Indian Economy), the correct option is (C).

questions.questionText: The `Hindu growth rate' is a term used to refer to -

options.text: the high rate of growth achieved after the new economic policy of 1991
the low rate of economic growth of India from the 1950s to the 1980s, which averaged around 3.5 per cent per year
the low growth of the economy during British period marked by an average of 3.5 percent
the growth rate of the country because India is referred to as `Hindustan'

questions.explanation: As per ICAI Study Material (Paper 4: Business Economics, Chapter 10: Indian Economy), the correct option is (B).

questions.questionText: In the context of the new economic policy of 1991, the term `disinvestment' stands for -

options.text: A policy whereby government investments are reduced to correct fiscal deficit
The policy of sale of portion of the government shareholding of a public sector enterprise
The policy of public partnership in private enterprise
A policy of opening up government monopoly to the privates sector

questions.explanation: As per ICAI Study Material (Paper 4: Business Economics, Chapter 10: Indian Economy), the correct option is (B).

to provide for the control of monopolies
to prohibit monopolistic and restrictive trade practice
all the above

grow more crops by redistributing land to landless people
High yielding varieties of seeds and scientific cultivation
Diversification to horticulture

Institutional reforms such as land reforms

All the above

A shift from state led industrialization to private sector led industrialisation
an expanded role for the public sector and licensing to the private sector
an expanded role of private sector a limited role of public sector

social and economic redistribution and industrialization directed by the state
